note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 29-year-old woman with 7 days of fever, sweats, myalgia, and malaise after recent return from Vietnam; requires further evaluation for possible travel-related or infectious etiology.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Ongoing fever for 7 days, feeling hot and sweaty "all the time," malaise.
- Onset/duration: Began 7 days ago; symptoms persist.
- Progression: Ongoing, not significantly improved with over-the-counter antipyretics.
- Associated symptoms: Generalized muscle aches, nausea (reduced appetite), fatigue, sweating (including night sweats alternating with chills), minimal oral intake, no significant relief with ibuprofen/paracetamol.
- Pertinent negatives: No cough, cold symptoms, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, rash, significant change in headaches, no new joint pain (baseline back pain only), no urinary symptoms.
- Review of systems: Headaches longstanding; associated with screen use and weather change, no change in pattern. No known migraines currently. Back pain is chronic and attributed to posture.
- Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; trip included rural travel, trekking, cycling, exposure to farmlands, rivers, and cities. Malaria prophylaxis taken (daily regimen, name not recalled).
- No recent sick contacts or similar reported illnesses in contacts.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain: Attributed to prolonged sitting and poor posture, under physiotherapy.
- No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
- Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Ibuprofen (over-the-counter; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Paracetamol (over-the-counter; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Pollen allergy (hay fever); no drug allergies.

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse, currently struggling to work due to fatigue.
- Smoking: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake, "not too much."
- Exercise: Moderate activity several times per week.

Family History:
- Father died of heart attack at age 68.
- No other family history noted.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed during this consult (remote).

Investigations:
- None performed yet.
- Planned: Blood tests including thick and thin blood films for malaria, inflammatory markers.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Fever of unknown origin post-travel (Vietnam)
  - Differential includes malaria, other tropical infections, and general infectious causes.
  - Plan: In-person clinic visit for physical examination.
  - Plan: Blood tests including thick and thin blood films (malaria screen), inflammatory markers, other relevant investigations as guided by examination.
  - Advice: Avoid work until diagnosis clarified.
  - Advised urgent evaluation.
- Issue 2: Chronic back pain (stable/known)
  - Under physiotherapy currently; no acute concerns raised at this visit.
- General Plan:
  - Patient to attend central London clinic for urgent assessment and testing.
  - Option to attend local A&E if clinic attendance not feasible.
  - Clinician to notify admin for booking, information for reception provided.
  - Work fitness note implied until further work-up complete.
  - Advised follow-up determined by examination and investigation results.

Quality checks (document_quality):

●	Missing but clinically expected elements: Physical exam (as consult remote), medication details (dose/route/frequency), full malaria prophylaxis history (medication name), full systems review (e.g., GI, respiratory, neurological not exhaustively covered).
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality comment: Transcript clear and well-organized; minimal noise/inaudible segments; adequate detail for clinical assessment.
